directorStatement.audienceFeeling: It feels awful when you say something wrong and everyone hears it. Even after class moves on, your stomach can still feel stuck in the bad moment.
directorStatement.emotionalChange: Let the audience feel the blush before the magic begins: embarrassment as a physical freeze, not a lesson. Keep this quiet and recognisable; the drama is in the mismatch between Jenny’s nod and the truth of her posture.
directorStatement.theLaugh: Jenny wants to read the sentence correctly and get safely through her turn. Jenny wants the moment to be over and for nobody to look closely at her hurt. She needs to know that a visible mistake does not reduce her worth. She needs permission to admit she is not all right without becoming the mistake.
directorStatement.visualSurprise: Jenny stands in the exposed classroom space and tries to read the line. The ordinary word on the board becomes dangerous through silence, hesitation and the accidental wrong word. The tiny laugh is not cruelly staged, but it is enough to make Jenny’s body close around the worksheet and make her corr -> Jenny holding her bag, the folded worksheet hidden inside.
directorStatement.carryForward: Jenny has hidden the feeling instead of sharing it, carrying the shame forward.

northStar.surfaceStory: Jenny is asked to read aloud. The word on the board trips her, the room goes very still, and the mistake feels bigger than the classroom. She wants the moment to pass without being seen in it.
northStar.universalTruth: A small mistake can feel like it changes how others see you, especially when everyone is looking.
northStar.childClearWant: Jenny wants to get the word right and stop the attention before it sticks.
northStar.emotionalNeed: To feel that being wrong is survivable and does not make her small.
northStar.falseBeliefUnderPressure: If I say the wrong thing, everyone will remember only that.
northStar.relationshipEngine: The teacher’s steady kindness gives Jenny a way back, while the nearby classmate’s simple check-in shows that connection can survive embarrassment.
northStar.ordinaryLifeTruth: When you are put on the spot, your body can close up faster than your thinking can catch up.
northStar.sceneTurn: The mistake moves from being a public problem to something Jenny can answer again, with support still present.
audienceJourney: Recognition: that horrible quiet when a word gets stuck
Tension: the body tightening around the page
Relief: an adult does not make the moment worse
Shift: the wrong answer is not treated as the whole story
Aftertaste: shaky, but no longer alone
northStar.finalAfterFeeling: A little embarrassed, but steadier and more able to try again.
northStar.dialogueSubtractionOpportunity: Let silence, the paper grip, and the tiny pause carry the shame; the dialogue can stay plain and brief.
northStar.environmentPressure: The classroom’s exposed front space, the quiet of the room, and the waiting eyes turn an ordinary reading into pressure.

transformation.entryBelief: If I get it wrong, I will feel small in front of everyone.
transformation.entryFeeling: Exposed, embarrassed, and suddenly very alone.
transformation.pressureBehaviour: She folds in on herself, clutches the worksheet, and tries to shrink the moment with a quick escape answer.
transformation.costlyChoice: She hides the feeling instead of asking for help or taking a breath with the room.
transformation.exitBelief: Being wrong is not the same as being small.
transformation.exitAction: She tries the word again, out loud, while still being seen.

tapestry.physicalMotif: The worksheet and the written word becoming smaller or bigger against the fixed classroom space.
tapestry.sonicMotif: A held room tone, then a tiny scrape of paper or chair that feels louder than it should.
tapestry.colourAndLightProgression: Neutral classroom light at first, then slightly cooler and flatter at the peak of embarrassment, easing back into steadier warmth once she tries again.
tapestry.thematicVisualContrast: Big public space versus small body; the board’s single word versus Jenny’s tightened grip on the paper.
tapestry.openingClosingRhyme: Open on Jenny standing at the front with the worksheet; close on the same shared classroom space, but now the word can be said again without the room swallowing her.

creativeIntent.governingAudienceExperience: It feels awful when you say something wrong and everyone hears it. Even after class moves on, your stomach can still feel stuck in the bad moment.
creativeIntent.scenePurpose: Show Jenny’s public reading stumble and the feeling staying with her afterward.
creativeIntent.emotionalPointOfView: Let the audience feel the blush before the magic begins: embarrassment as a physical freeze, not a lesson. Keep this quiet and recognisable; the drama is in the mismatch between Jenny’s nod and the truth of her posture.
creativeIntent.comicOrDramaticMechanism: Jenny wants to read the sentence correctly and get safely through her turn. Jenny wants the moment to be over and for nobody to look closely at her hurt. She needs to know that a visible mistake does not reduce her worth. She needs permission to admit she is not all right without becoming the mistake.
creativeIntent.characterPerformanceStrategy: A small public stumble can become disproportionately huge inside a sensitive child, even when the adults respond gently. The polite ‘I’m fine’ masks the real emotional event: Jenny is beginning to hide rather than process the shame.
creativeIntent.visualGrammar: Fixed 30-second shots, one keyframe each, as the writer broke them down: Shot 01 "Reading Goes Wrong" (30s): Jenny stands in the exposed classroom space and tries to read the line. The ordinary word on the board becomes dangerous through silence, hesitation and the accidental wrong word. The tiny laugh is not cruelly staged, but it is enough to make Jenny’s body close around the worksheet and make her corrected answer come out small.; Shot 02 "The Feeling Stays" (30s): Back at her desk, Jenny is no longer at the front of the room, but the feeling has stayed in front of her. She folds the worksheet smaller and answers a kind check-in with a tiny false assurance, choosing concealment over connection before the school bell releases her with the shame hidden in her bag.
creativeIntent.cameraCharacterRelationship: Chosen by the shot conference inside each fixed unit; the writer names the frame, not the camera.
creativeIntent.movementVersusStillness: Each unit holds its full length: the written action, then the silent acting and landing the writer's Final Frame asks for — never dead air, never invented events.
creativeIntent.rhythmAndEscalation: Reading Goes Wrong -> The Feeling Stays
creativeIntent.cutPhilosophy: A cut only at the writer's shot boundaries; every 30-second unit is one continuous provider request.
creativeIntent.openingImage: Jenny stands in the exposed classroom space and tries to read the line. The ordinary word on the board becomes dangerous through silence, hesitation and the accidental wrong word. The tiny laugh is not cruelly staged, but it is enough to make Jenny’s body close around the worksheet and make her corr
creativeIntent.closingImage: Jenny holding her bag, the folded worksheet hidden inside.
creativeIntent.handoverToNextScene: Jenny has hidden the feeling instead of sharing it, carrying the shame forward.
creativeIntent.intendedFinalFeeling: A warm, private courage: the feeling is still remembered, but it is no longer bigger than Jenny.

emotion.entryState: Exposed and trying to perform normally.
emotion.pressure: The silent classroom front space and the waiting line make the word feel dangerous.
emotion.choiceOrRealisation: She keeps going after the hesitation and then answers again when corrected.
emotion.exitState: Embarrassed and smaller, but still present.
emotion.observableEvidence: Jenny pauses, says the wrong word, receives the correction, and then repeats the right word with a reduced, tight delivery.
emotion.heldAfterBeat: The memory of being heard wrong, and the wish to disappear into the page.

comedy.mechanism: A tiny verbal misread against a very ordinary sentence.
comedy.setup: Jenny begins a simple read-aloud in a quiet room.
comedy.expectation: The class expects a routine answer and then to move on.
comedy.button: The Teacher calmly says, 'That’s all right. Try again.'

emotion.entryState: Embarrassed and still trying to look normal.
emotion.pressure: The feeling of being watched lingers even after she returns to her desk.
emotion.choiceOrRealisation: She chooses concealment over honesty when a classmate checks on her.
emotion.exitState: Shut down, polite, and carrying the shame alone.
emotion.observableEvidence: Jenny folds the worksheet smaller, answers 'Yeah.' too quickly, and keeps the feeling off her face.
emotion.heldAfterBeat: The hidden worksheet, the unanswered check-in, and the lingering heat of embarrassment.

comedy.mechanism: No comic turn; the beat stays in the quiet after the mistake.
comedy.setup: A classmate notices Jenny and asks if she is all right.
comedy.expectation: A small honest answer might open the moment back up.
comedy.disruption: Jenny gives a tiny false assurance instead.
comedy.hold: A brief pause on Jenny folding the worksheet smaller lets the discomfort settle.

shots.purpose: Deliver the full public embarrassment beat: a simple classroom read that turns painful when the wrong word is heard aloud.
shots.performanceAssignment: Performance phases: anticipation: Jenny She looks between the worksheet and the board, and her hands tighten on the paper before she speaks; action: Jenny She reads, stalls, and then says the wrong word aloud before trying again; reaction: Jenny Her shoulders fold inward, her grip pulls the worksheet close, and her answer comes back smaller; settle: ENVIRONMENT The classroom stays still around her as the moment lands and holds. Cause and effect: The quiet room and waiting line make Jenny’s hesitation readable; the wrong word triggers a visible shrink in her posture and a tighter hold on the page. Visible turn: A routine read turns into public embarrassment, then into a smaller, guarded retry. Land on: Jenny remains at the front, visibly embarrassed, with the worksheet held close after her tiny corrected answer. Acting freedom: Keep the room calm and let the comedy or hurt come from timing, not extra reaction. Allow small eye flicks, breath catches, and paper tremor, but keep the overall shape simple and readable.

shots.openingPose: Jenny stands at the front of the classroom with her worksheet open while the board word is visible across from her and the room waits.
shots.cutInMotivation: This shot opens on the classroom reading keyframe and stays with that public moment all the way through the mistake and retry; cutting earlier would weaken the lived experience of the shame landing.
shots.dialogueBinding: Teacher's vocal beat performs per the approved voice design.

physicalStaging.payoffShape: The teacher completes her walk and comes to rest beside the board exactly as her calm line lands; Jenny's small retry follows with the teacher still standing there.

shots.principalPerformanceApproved: Jenny tries to keep reading, stalls on the word, says the wrong one, then answers again in a smaller voice after the teacher’s calm prompt.
shots.physicalPerformanceApproved: Jenny stands at the front with the worksheet held in both hands, eyes moving from the page to the board. She starts the line, slows on the troublesome word, then stops with her fingers tightening on the paper. After the wrong word lands, her shoulders draw in, the worksheet lifts closer to her chest, and she gives a small, careful retry while still half-folded into herself.
shots.animationTimingApproved: Begin steady and open, with a patient hold on the quiet before the stumble. Let the pause stretch just enough for the room to feel it, then let the wrong word trigger a quick inward collapse in posture. Keep the correction and tiny retry compact, with a short afterbeat so the embarrassment reads before the shot settles.

performanceBudgetApproved.rationale: The beat contains one continuous public-reading performance with one visible prop state change and two emotional turns: confidence to freeze, then freeze to tiny retry. It can live honestly in 30 seconds without splitting.

storyIntentApproved.narrativeFunction: Introduce the shame event through a public reading mistake.
storyIntentApproved.outerAction: Jenny reads aloud, misreads the word, hears the correction, and tries again.
storyIntentApproved.innerAction: She tries to stay composed while feeling herself shrink.
storyIntentApproved.performanceDirection: Start bravely, let the pause get too long, make the wrong word sound smaller than she hoped, and let the retry stay tight and careful.
storyIntentApproved.mutedRead: A child stands at the front, hesitates, makes a wrong read, gets corrected kindly, and retries while visibly shrinking.
storyIntentApproved.environmentPressure: The exposed front-of-class space and quiet listening room make every syllable feel public.
storyIntentApproved.soundStory: Room tone should do most of the pressure; the tiny laugh and the teacher’s calm line should land plainly, not musically padded.
storyIntentApproved.motifUse: The worksheet feels like it has become heavier in Jenny’s hands, making the page itself carry the embarrassment.
storyIntentApproved.thoughtChangeAndCut: The cut inside the unit should only happen if the thought changes from trying to read to realizing everyone heard the mistake; otherwise hold.
storyIntentApproved.mustUnderstand: Jenny said the wrong word and felt the room hear it.
storyIntentApproved.mustNotKnowYet: Do not soften the hurt into a lesson or resolve it into confidence yet.
storyIntentApproved.reactionBeat: The tiny laugh changes the meaning by making the mistake social, not merely private.
storyIntentApproved.relationshipDistance: At arm’s-length public distance from classmates, with the teacher steady but not rescuing.
storyIntentApproved.relationshipPowerDynamic: The room has the power of attention; the teacher’s calm response gives Jenny a narrow path back.
storyIntentApproved.touchOrAvoidance: Avoidance dominates; Jenny clutches the worksheet instead of reaching out.
storyIntentApproved.eyelineRule: Jenny looks to the page and board, then briefly up when corrected, but cannot hold the room’s gaze for long.
storyIntentApproved.silhouetteRead: Her shoulders curl inward around the sheet, making the body read smaller than the classroom space.
storyIntentApproved.silenceRule: Protect the quiet before the mistake and the beat after it; those silences are the embarrassment.
storyIntentApproved.scoreInstruction: No score needed over the reading itself; if present at all, it should stay nearly absent and never rescue the moment.

storyboardStagePlanApproved.purpose: Establish the public reading pressure and let the sentence begin cleanly before the stumble lands.
storyboardStagePlanApproved.primaryEvent: Jenny stands at the front, starts the line, and the room holds still around the word on the board.
storyboardStagePlanApproved.emotionalOrComicTurn: Normal classroom attention turns into exposed pressure.
storyboardStagePlanApproved.cameraAndTransition: PLANNED_CUT into the unit on the shared front-of-room keyframe; keep the camera steady and slightly withheld while the room silence does the work.
storyboardStagePlanApproved.observableEndState: Jenny is mid-read with the worksheet in hand and the board word looming in the same frame.

storyboardStagePlanApproved.purpose: Carry the hesitation into the wrong word and let the tiny social ripple register without widening the scene beyond its honest size.
storyboardStagePlanApproved.primaryEvent: Jenny pauses, says 'Briggle,' and a tiny laugh follows while her body tightens around the paper.
storyboardStagePlanApproved.emotionalOrComicTurn: The mistake becomes publicly audible; embarrassment snaps shut around her posture.
storyboardStagePlanApproved.cameraAndTransition: Hold the same axis, then make a small, motivated push closer only as the wrong word lands, so the frame feels the room narrowing rather than the camera showing off.
storyboardStagePlanApproved.observableEndState: Jenny has curled inward over the worksheet and the laugh has already passed through the room.

storyboardStagePlanApproved.purpose: Let the teacher’s correction and Jenny’s tiny retry land as the sad, small aftermath of the mistake.
storyboardStagePlanApproved.primaryEvent: The teacher WALKS INTO FRAME from the side of the room - a visible, unhurried walk across the floor - and arrives beside the board as she says 'That's all right. Try again.'; Jenny answers 'Bridge.' with a reduced voice.
storyboardStagePlanApproved.emotionalOrComicTurn: Kindness arrives, but shame still shrinks the answer.
storyboardStagePlanApproved.cameraAndTransition: Remain continuous and patient; the teacher's entrance is an on-screen walk that the camera lets happen in the same shot (she is not in frame before it and never pops or appears between frames), then hold just long enough for the corrected word to feel fragile; no cut is needed because the emotional turn is still inside the same public moment.
storyboardStagePlanApproved.observableEndState: Jenny is still standing, still embarrassed, with the worksheet held close and her voice diminished; the teacher now stands calmly beside the board, having walked in.

source.title: Dreamina Seedance 2.5 User Guide
source.scope: Official Dreamina/BytePlus prompt guidance; executable API schema, pricing and account access are separate

guideSemantics.timestampControl: Time ranges allocate pacing and exact time points improve alignment; they are not a frame-accurate edit guarantee.
guideSemantics.extensionPreservation: Preserve the source and match its boundary state, but review the join; generated continuation and boundary frames are not guaranteed pixel-identical.
guideSemantics.negativeInstructions: Explicit forbidden items improve reliability but remain probabilistic and require review.
guideSemantics.identityStability: Multi-character consistency is improved, not self-approving; identity and count still require visual review.
guideSemantics.longVideoRoute: The 5-180 second mode is a Dreamina beta product capability, not a qualified Studio API route.
guideSemantics.audioOnly: Dreamina product guidance describes audio-only creation; the current BytePlus Seedance 2.0 API still requires at least one image or video reference.
guideSemantics.cleanOutput: Dreamina advertises cleaner 4K output; the executable provider contract remains the authority for resolution and every render still requires QC.
guideSemantics.watermarkPolicy: The Studio never uses generative watermark removal as a production shortcut; source footage must be owned or licensed and delivered clean.

guideSemantics.timestampControl: Time ranges allocate pacing and exact time points improve alignment; they are not a frame-accurate edit guarantee.
guideSemantics.extensionPreservation: Preserve the source and match its boundary state, but review the join; generated continuation and boundary frames are not guaranteed pixel-identical.
guideSemantics.negativeInstructions: Explicit forbidden items improve reliability but remain probabilistic and require review.
guideSemantics.identityStability: Multi-character consistency is improved, not self-approving; identity and count still require visual review.
guideSemantics.longVideoRoute: The 5-180 second mode is a Dreamina beta product capability, not a qualified Studio API route.
guideSemantics.audioOnly: Dreamina product guidance describes audio-only creation; the current BytePlus Seedance 2.0 API still requires at least one image or video reference.
guideSemantics.cleanOutput: Dreamina advertises cleaner 4K output; the executable provider contract remains the authority for resolution and every render still requires QC.
guideSemantics.watermarkPolicy: The Studio never uses generative watermark removal as a production shortcut; source footage must be owned or licensed and delivered clean.

source.title: Dreamina Seedance 2.5 User Guide
source.scope: Official Dreamina/BytePlus prompt guidance; executable API schema, pricing and account access are separate

guideSemantics.timestampControl: Time ranges allocate pacing and exact time points improve alignment; they are not a frame-accurate edit guarantee.
guideSemantics.extensionPreservation: Preserve the source and match its boundary state, but review the join; generated continuation and boundary frames are not guaranteed pixel-identical.
guideSemantics.negativeInstructions: Explicit forbidden items improve reliability but remain probabilistic and require review.
guideSemantics.identityStability: Multi-character consistency is improved, not self-approving; identity and count still require visual review.
guideSemantics.longVideoRoute: The 5-180 second mode is a Dreamina beta product capability, not a qualified Studio API route.
guideSemantics.audioOnly: Dreamina product guidance describes audio-only creation; the current BytePlus Seedance 2.0 API still requires at least one image or video reference.
guideSemantics.cleanOutput: Dreamina advertises cleaner 4K output; the executable provider contract remains the authority for resolution and every render still requires QC.
guideSemantics.watermarkPolicy: The Studio never uses generative watermark removal as a production shortcut; source footage must be owned or licensed and delivered clean.

source.title: Dreamina Seedance 2.5 User Guide
source.scope: Official Dreamina/BytePlus prompt guidance; executable API schema, pricing and account access are separate

guideSemantics.timestampControl: Time ranges allocate pacing and exact time points improve alignment; they are not a frame-accurate edit guarantee.
guideSemantics.extensionPreservation: Preserve the source and match its boundary state, but review the join; generated continuation and boundary frames are not guaranteed pixel-identical.
guideSemantics.negativeInstructions: Explicit forbidden items improve reliability but remain probabilistic and require review.
guideSemantics.identityStability: Multi-character consistency is improved, not self-approving; identity and count still require visual review.
guideSemantics.longVideoRoute: The 5-180 second mode is a Dreamina beta product capability, not a qualified Studio API route.
guideSemantics.audioOnly: Dreamina product guidance describes audio-only creation; the current BytePlus Seedance 2.0 API still requires at least one image or video reference.
guideSemantics.cleanOutput: Dreamina advertises cleaner 4K output; the executable provider contract remains the authority for resolution and every render still requires QC.
guideSemantics.watermarkPolicy: The Studio never uses generative watermark removal as a production shortcut; source footage must be owned or licensed and delivered clean.

inputs.title: The Box That Felt Small
inputs.logline: After Jenny hides the shame of misreading a word, Patch leads the Box Monsters into a shoebox classroom where a giant mistake must become something she can try again with, not something that makes her small.

orderedEvents.text: Jenny stands at the front of the classroom holding her worksheet.
The word BRIDGE is written on the board.
Jenny looks at the word. Her fingers tighten around the paper.
One child lets out a tiny laugh. Another child laughs because the first one did.
Jenny looks at the word again. It feels much bigger now.
Final Frame: Jenny frozen, embarrassed, holding the worksheet close.

beats.storyBeat: Jenny stands in the exposed classroom space and tries to read the line. The ordinary word on the board becomes dangerous through silence, hesitation and the accidental wrong word. The tiny laugh is not cruelly staged, but it is enough to make Jenny’s body close around the worksheet and make her corrected answer come out small.
beats.want: Jenny wants to read the sentence correctly and get safely through her turn.
beats.need: She needs to know that a visible mistake does not reduce her worth.
beats.kidRead: It feels awful when you say something wrong and everyone hears it.
beats.adultRead: A small public stumble can become disproportionately huge inside a sensitive child, even when the adults respond gently.
beats.emotionalIntent: Let the audience feel the blush before the magic begins: embarrassment as a physical freeze, not a lesson.

orderedEvents.text: Jenny is back at her desk.
The class has moved on, but Jenny has not.
The worksheet lies in front of her. The word BRIDGE seems to stare back.
Jenny slowly folds the paper smaller and smaller.
She slips the folded worksheet into her school bag.
Final Frame: Jenny holding her bag, the folded worksheet hidden inside.

beats.storyBeat: Back at her desk, Jenny is no longer at the front of the room, but the feeling has stayed in front of her. She folds the worksheet smaller and answers a kind check-in with a tiny false assurance, choosing concealment over connection before the school bell releases her with the shame hidden in her bag.
beats.want: Jenny wants the moment to be over and for nobody to look closely at her hurt.
beats.need: She needs permission to admit she is not all right without becoming the mistake.
beats.kidRead: Even after class moves on, your stomach can still feel stuck in the bad moment.
beats.adultRead: The polite ‘I’m fine’ masks the real emotional event: Jenny is beginning to hide rather than process the shame.
beats.emotionalIntent: Keep this quiet and recognisable; the drama is in the mismatch between Jenny’s nod and the truth of her posture.

cuts.dialogue: Classmate: You all right?

cuts.action: She slips the folded worksheet into her school bag.
Final Frame: Jenny holding her bag, the folded worksheet hidden inside.

orderedEvents.text: Shot 03: The Feeling Goes Into The Box
Jenny kneels on her bedroom floor.
Her decorated shoebox sits beside her bed. It has stars, hearts and one wonky rainbow drawn on the lid.
Inside are small treasures: a ribbon, a pebble, an old badge, a folded card.
She places the folded worksheet inside the box.
For a moment, she keeps her hand on it.

orderedEvents.speaker: Jenny
orderedEvents.text: I don’t want to think about it.
The box gives the smallest cardboard sigh.
Final Frame: The closed shoebox on the bedroom floor.

beats.storyBeat: In her bedroom, Jenny brings the folded worksheet to her decorated shoebox, a safe place for treasured things. She tries to make the feeling disappear by placing it inside and closing the lid, not noticing that the box has received more than paper: it has received the feeling she cannot carry alone.
beats.want: Jenny wants to put the worksheet away and stop thinking about the classroom mistake.
beats.need: She needs the hidden feeling to be met, not buried.
beats.kidRead: Jenny hides the paper because looking at it hurts.
beats.adultRead: The shoebox becomes a child’s private emotional container: a tender coping strategy that also signals isolation.
beats.emotionalIntent: Make the action intimate and gentle, with the box feeling like a confidant even before the magic answers.

orderedEvents.text: Then the lid lifts by the tiniest amount.
A warm golden line glows through the gap.
A soft cardboard pulse travels from the box, under the bed, through the floorboards.
The glow moves like a little signal through the dark.
Final Frame: Golden light disappearing through the floor.

beats.storyBeat: Later, with Jenny asleep, the shoebox quietly opens just enough to send a warm golden signal through the dark. The folded worksheet trembles, and the room’s silence becomes a secret request for help moving from Jenny’s world toward The Fold.
beats.want: The shoebox wants to send the feeling call without waking Jenny.
beats.need: The hidden shame needs a safe responder.
beats.kidRead: The box knows Jenny needs help even though she is asleep.
beats.adultRead: The fantasy externalises emotional processing: care begins when the child is no longer consciously defending against the feeling.
beats.emotionalIntent: Shift from private sadness to wonder; this is the promise that hidden feelings are not abandoned.

beats.storyBeat: The Fold receives the call in the middle of Patch and Nib’s wobbly routine, turning comic imbalance into mission focus. The signal honk collapses Patch’s tower-of-calm act, but when Tilly reads the feeling as shame, the team’s stillness shows they understand the delicacy of what they are entering.
beats.want: The monsters want to identify the call and know where to go.
beats.need: They need to treat shame with care rather than with noise or bravado.
beats.kidRead: The funny cardboard city gets an alarm, and the monsters discover the feeling is serious.
beats.adultRead: The scene balances levity with respect: shame changes the team’s body language before anyone explains why it matters.
beats.emotionalIntent: Use comedy as an entry ramp, then let the word shame quiet the room.

The shoebox twitches, The Fold glows, Nib’s distant voice keeps the cafe joke alive, and Jenny’s smile carries the secret repair into warm black.

beats.adultRead: The healing is not amnesia; Jenny integrates the embarrassing moment by choosing when and how to mention it.
beats.emotionalIntent: End on modest triumph rather than applause: the final feeling is private confidence, shared kindness and a tiny hidden wink from The Fold.
